questions.q: Which of these is a passive process (needs no energy from respiration)?
options: Reabsorption of glucose in the kidney
Uptake of mineral ions by roots
Active transport of glucose in the gut
questions.explain: Osmosis (and diffusion) are passive; active transport requires energy.
Chromosomes are made of long DNA molecules that carry genes.

questions.q: Why does increasing temperature usually increase transpiration?
options: Water molecules evaporate and diffuse faster
questions.explain: Higher temperatures speed up evaporation and diffusion of water vapour from the leaf.

questions.q: From which chamber does oxygenated blood leave the heart into the aorta?
questions.explain: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta to the body.

questions.q: Which tissue transports water and mineral ions up the plant?
questions.explain: Xylem carries water and dissolved minerals upwards from the roots.

questions.q: In which direction(s) can phloem transport substances?
options: Both up and down the plant
questions.explain: Translocation in phloem can move dissolved food in both directions to where it is needed.

questions.q: Which part of the blood mainly transports dissolved substances such as carbon dioxide, urea and nutrients?
questions.explain: Plasma is the liquid that transports dissolved substances around the body.

questions.q: How are red blood cells adapted to carry oxygen?
options: They can change shape to engulf bacteria
They have a nucleus packed with DNA
They are biconcave and have no nucleus, giving more room for haemoglobin
questions.explain: Red blood cells lack a nucleus and are biconcave, maximising space and surface area for haemoglobin.

options: Water draining out of the soil
The flow of sugars in phloem
The movement of air through stomata
The continuous movement of water from roots up through the xylem to the leaves
questions.explain: As water evaporates from leaves, more is pulled up through the xylem in the transpiration stream.

options: The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant
The movement of sugars in phloem
questions.explain: Transpiration is the evaporation and loss of water vapour, mainly through the stomata of leaves.

questions.q: During which stage of the cell cycle do the chromosomes line up in the middle and separate to opposite ends of the cell?
questions.explain: In mitosis the duplicated chromosomes line up and are pulled to opposite poles before the cell divides.

questions.q: Compared with adult stem cells, embryonic stem cells can:
options: Differentiate into a wider range of cell types
questions.explain: Embryonic stem cells can form almost any cell type, whereas adult stem cells form a more limited range.
